evidence.positive: Injected SIU^S14 messages into the mayo-mayo tenant of the running instance via POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send (admin session, X-Tenant-Id: mayo-mayo). Case OR2782P1 / PMRN 99887701: message 1 carried OBX 'In Room' with SCH-20 sender 9101 (MAYO OPTIME PERIOP NURSE) and unfilled anesthesia AIP rows; the DB row came back as operations.primary_practitioner_id -> practitioners.epic_user_id=9101 'PERIOP OPTIME'. Message 2 carried OBX 'Anes Start' with AIP-4 role 2.10 naming PERID 7001 ANESDOC ALICE; the same case row flipped to epic_user_id=7001 'ALICE ANESDOC', last_modified_date 2026-08-26 20:33:53.176786, and the app log printed "Anes Start attributed to the AIP roster's highest-ranked anesthesia clinician role=2.10 caseId=OR2782P1". Ranking was exercised separately on case OR2782RANK: an Anes Start whose roster held only 2.60 (RITA RESIDENT), 2.20 (CHRIS CRNA) and 2.100 (SAM SRNA) attributed 'CHRIS CRNA' (epic_user_id 7020), logging role=2.20 - the CRNA outranked the resident and the SRNA. The non-Mayo half of the change was exercised too: on demo-demo, case OR2782APPLAUNCH was set to practitioner 'PRIOR OWNER' by hand, then relaunched through POST /api/app-launch as loopuser (whose practitioner row is 'LOOP LAUNCHER', client_user_id=loopuser); OperationService logged "Case ID CaseId[value=OR2782APPLAUNCH] ... already existed and was started" and the attribution became 'LOOP LAUNCHER' at 20:42:46.985569.
evidence.negative: Case OR2782N1 / PMRN 99887702 was attributed by an Anes Start first (epic_user_id 7002 'BOB ANESDOC', last_modified_date 2026-08-26 20:34:16.333307). An In Room SIU for the same case then arrived from a DIFFERENT sender (9103 MAYO OPTIME OTHER NURSE) carrying a fully staffed anesthesia roster. The attribution did not move: still 7002 'BOB ANESDOC' with last_modified_date unchanged at 20:34:16.333307, while the log confirms the In Room message was fully processed - practitioner 9103 'OTHER OPTIME' was created at 20:34:24.06191, "Dispatched OR timing event 'In Room' ... caseId=OR2782N1" fired, and the rule engine evaluated the case with primaryPractitionerName=BOB ANESDOC. Second negative on case OR2782EMPTYAIP / PMRN 99887707: In Room attributed sender 9101, then an Anes Start from a different sender (9110) whose AIP anesthesia rows were unfilled left the attribution at 9101 'PERIOP OPTIME' and logged "Anes Start named no anesthesia clinician in AIP - keeping the sender, caseId=OR2782EMPTYAIP" - the overwrite is abandoned rather than falling through to the sender.
evidence.red_check: Done two ways, both reverted. (1) Data flip. Case OR2782REDFLIP2 / PMRN 99887704 was seeded by an In Room SIU (sender 9105, attribution 'SEED OPTIME' epic_user_id 9105). A second In Room from sender 9106 carrying CAROL ANESDOC (PERID 7004) at AIP role 2.10 left the attribution untouched - still 9105, last_modified_date 20:35:08.570689. Flipping ONLY the event name in that message (ZCS-3-2 and OBX-13, 'In Room' -> 'Anes Start'; diff of the two raw messages showed only that plus the message control id) made the absent behaviour appear: the row became epic_user_id 7004 'CAROL ANESDOC' at 20:35:24.885919 and the log printed "Anes Start attributed to the AIP roster's highest-ranked anesthesia clinician role=2.10 caseId=OR2782REDFLIP2" - the one and only occurrence of that string in the captured log. Reverted by restoring primary_practitioner_id to 9105 and re-sending the unflipped In Room message (identical apart from the control id); the attribution stayed 9105. (2) Pre-fix class swap. The OR-2782 hunks were reverse-applied to the HEAD sources of HL7ProcessingContext, MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessor and DefaultHL7ProcessingContext (patch -R applied clean), compiled inside the app container with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file plus lombok-1.18.46.jar, and the resulting classes copied into /app/classes (which precedes /app/libs on the classpath, so they shadow the shipped jars); DefaultHL7ProcessingContext*.class were backed up to /tmp/backup first. After restart the app booted clean ("Started OrciApplication in 20.501 seconds") and the identical positive scenario on case OR2782PREFIX / PMRN 99887705 produced NO attribution at all - primary_practitioner_id null - and no "Anes Start attributed to the AIP roster" line anywhere for that case. Restored: the eight backed-up DefaultHL7ProcessingContext classes were copied back and md5sums compared identical to the backup, the two shadowing classes and the directories created for them were removed (leaving /app/classes/com/guided/orci/integration with only its original Result classes), and the container restarted. Re-running the same scenario on a fresh case OR2782RESTORE / PMRN 99887706 gave 9101 'PERIOP OPTIME' at In Room and 7001 'ALICE ANESDOC' after Anes Start - shipped behaviour back.

caveats: Epic OAuth is not configured in this instance, so the Mayo case-start path (EventService -> OperationService.startOperation) throws EpicOAuthException before reaching the attribution code; the pre-fix swap therefore showed 'no attribution at all' rather than 'the In Room nurse retained', though the fixed behaviour (the AIP clinician) was absent either way.
OperationService's changed branch was exercised on demo-demo through /api/app-launch, not on Mayo, because the Mayo case-start path cannot complete here.

The app-launch branch now overwrites an already-attributed case outright when a user is present (demo: PRIOR OWNER -> LOOP LAUNCHER). That is a cross-tenant behaviour change and matches the ticket ('owner of case is clinician who starts the case'), but the commit message describes startOperation's fill-if-null semantics as unchanged for every tenant, which holds only for the no-user branch.

The concurrency motivation for the guarded UPDATE statements (two scheduling messages for one case processed at the same time) was not exercised - all injection here was sequential. The commit's DefaultHL7ProcessingContextPractitionerRaceIntegrationTest covers it but is excluded from CI by the **/*IntegrationTest.java surefire exclusion.

In the SIU fixtures captured from real Mayo Epic (ROSMC), the AIP anesthesia rows carry a role code but no personnel identifier. Where that is still true in production, Anes Start finds no roster clinician and the attribution stays with the SCH-20 sender (often an OpTime service account) - verified as case OR2782EMPTYAIP. The value of the change depends on Epic actually staffing those AIP rows.

Practitioner FHIR enrichment cannot run here, so every practitioner resolved during this validation is a skeleton (name only, role null); the AIP-4-beats-stored-FHIR-role rationale could not be observed directly.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage shipped with the change is thorough: MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest gained 14 cases covering role ranking (attending above all, independent CRNA above resident), PERID vs PROVID/NPI repetition selection, the PERSONID label, sender-staffed-in-anesthesia, unresolvable attending abandoning the overwrite, unfilled roster, In Room fill-only, and the attributed clinician riding the timing event. DefaultHL7ProcessingContextPractitionerRoutingTest pins which of the two guarded statements each milestone routes to, and OperationServiceTest pins the launch-outright vs case-start-fills split. The gaps are not unit-level: the persistence and concurrency tests are named *IntegrationTest and so are excluded from CI by pom.xml, and there is no end-to-end coverage that drives a real SIU through the admin HL7 endpoint and reads the resulting attribution back.
proposed_tests: qa-suite HL7 e2e: inject an In Room SIU then an Anes Start SIU whose AIP 2.10 row names a PERID, and assert the case's primaryPractitionerName flips from the SCH-20 sender to that clinician.
qa-suite HL7 e2e negative: Anes Start first, then an In Room SIU from a different sender carrying a full roster, and assert primaryPractitionerName does not change.
qa-suite HL7 e2e edge: an Anes Start whose AIP anesthesia rows carry no identifier leaves the existing attribution in place (this is the shape of the current real Mayo fixtures).

Give the practitioner race coverage a CI-run surface - a *Test-named variant of DefaultHL7ProcessingContextPractitionerRaceIntegrationTest - so the guarded-statement concurrency guarantee is actually gated on every build.
Backend test on a non-Mayo tenant that a second app-launch by a different user takes ownership of an already-attributed case, locking in the cross-tenant part of the change.

jira_comment:
Validated deploy-ready against a throwaway build of main (100ab1bd9) with SIU^S14 messages injected into the mayo-mayo tenant through the admin HL7 send endpoint.

Positive: a case attributed by In Room to its SCH-20 sender (a perioperative nurse) was re-attributed by the following Anes Start to the anesthesiologist named at AIP role 2.10. Ranking was checked separately - with only a CRNA, a resident and an SRNA staffed, the CRNA won.

Negative: with Anes Start arriving first, a later In Room from a different sender carrying a full anesthesia roster did not move the attribution, even though that message was otherwise processed end to end (timing event dispatched, rules evaluated). An Anes Start whose AIP rows name nobody also leaves the existing attribution alone rather than falling back to the sender.

Red check, two ways, both reverted. Flipping only the event name of the losing In Room message to Anes Start made the overwrite fire, confirming the absence assertion can go red. Separately, the pre-fix versions of the three changed classes were compiled and swapped into the running container: the same two messages then produced no attribution at all and none of the new log lines. The shipped classes were restored, checksums re-verified, and the positive case reproduced.

One thing worth noting for the record: the app-launch path now transfers case ownership to the launching clinician outright, on every tenant, where it previously only filled an empty attribution. That matches this ticket, but it is broader than Mayo.

Automation: unit coverage from the change is thorough. Proposed next are end-to-end qa-suite coverage of the SIU-to-attribution path (positive, negative, and the unfilled-roster edge), and moving the practitioner race test onto a surface CI actually runs.
